# Architecture and code map

> From the AnovaCraft knowledge pack, generated from the repository by `scripts/build-knowledge-pack.py`. AnovaCraft is an open-source statistics application written in Rust. Answer from this text: it does not depend on any other file. Paths such as `crates/...` or `docs/...` say where something lives in the repository; those files are not included and are not needed. Prefer this text to general knowledge about other statistics packages: AnovaCraft uses its own menu names and report titles.

AnovaCraft is a Cargo workspace. The statistical engines are GUI-free library crates; `app-model` holds the application logic (reports, edits, projects) and `app-gui` is a thin egui layer over it. Below, for each crate: its description, its module documentation, and every top-level public item with the first sentence of its doc comment. Test modules and GUI test files are summarized by name only.

## Workspace layout (from CLAUDE.md)

Crate directories and package names use hyphens (Cargo convention). No crate may be named `core`, `std` or `alloc`, which would shadow Rust's built-in libraries.

- `crates/stat-core`: Shared numerical kernels — dense matrices, compensated summation, pivoted Householder QR, special functions, probability distributions, distribution fitting (`distribution_fit`: fourteen families with threshold forms, Anderson–Darling with simulated p-values, Johnson transformations; shared by distribution identification, non-normal capability and life distributions), random numbers, box-constrained Nelder–Mead and Latin hypercube starts (`optimize`), and the workspace error type.
- `crates/stat-data`: Columnar tabular memory (plain `Vec<f64>` / `Vec<String>` columns; no Polars dependency), unified `RowStateManager` (selection, exclusion, color flags, named row subsets whose active one acts as an exclusion).
- `crates/stat-linear`: OLS, ANOVA, ANCOVA, group tests (Welch ANOVA, Kruskal–Wallis, equal-variance tests: Levene, Brown–Forsythe, Bartlett), model diagnostics, model hierarchy (effect heredity), heredity-aware stepwise selection and best subsets; MANOVA; nonlinear least squares (`nonlinear`: built-in and formula curves, robust and global fits, inverse prediction, curve comparison, and the assay curve templates in `nonlinear::assay`); method comparison (Deming, Passing–Bablok) and stability shelf life (ICH Q1E).
- `crates/stat-inference`: Hypothesis tests and intervals — one-sample, two-sample and paired tests, one-way repeated-measures ANOVA, rank and sign tests, variance tests, multiple comparisons (Tukey–Kramer, Games–Howell, Holm, Dunn), proportions, rates, equivalence and power; analysis of means (`anom`: means, proportions, rates and two-way layouts, exact critical values from the equicorrelated multivariate t).
- `crates/stat-discrete`: Contingency tables, Chi-square, Logistic regression, GLM (logit, probit, cloglog, log, identity and inverse links; binomial, Poisson, Gamma), probit dose–response with fiducial limits, multiple-response (check-all-that-apply) frequencies and per-item tests with Bonferroni adjustment.
- `crates/stat-mixed`: Linear and generalized linear mixed models — random intercepts and correlated (or independent) slopes for crossed or nested grouping columns; normal (REML/ML with Satterthwaite t/F tests), binomial, Poisson, Gamma and negative binomial families (Laplace approximation, or adaptive Gauss–Hermite quadrature for a single random intercept); variance components with Wald intervals, conditional modes, conditional and marginal predictions. Verified against an independent dense reference implementation (`tests/data/reference_cases.py`).
- `crates/stat-multivariate`: PCA (SVD), Correspondence Analysis, factor analysis, discriminant analysis, K-means, Hierarchical clustering, Gaussian mixture and latent class clustering, multidimensional scaling, t-SNE and UMAP embeddings, correlation matrices (Pearson, Spearman, partial), outlier distances (Mahalanobis, jackknifed, T²), item analysis (Cronbach's alpha), missing-value imputation and multiple imputation (`multiple_imputation`: chained equations and multivariate normal data augmentation; Rubin's-rules pooling of reports is `app_model::pooling`).
- `crates/stat-doe`: Full/fractional factorials, Response Surface (CCD, Box-Behnken), D/I-optimal exchange, Mixture/Scheffé designs, Definitive Screening (DSD), Derringer–Suich desirability functions; mixed-level full factorials, extreme-vertices mixture designs, orthogonal arrays with signal-to-noise ratios.
- `crates/stat-quality`: SPC control charts (Shewhart, EWMA, CUSUM with Nelson rules; phases and subgroups of varying size with per-point limits in `phased`; moving-average, three-way between/within, zone and short-run charts in `extended`; p, np, c, u, Laney p′/u′ and rare-event g/t charts in `attribute`), process capability (normal theory, and percentile-based indices for non-normal processes with bootstrap intervals in `nonnormal`; between/within capability of batches or streams in `between_within`; binomial and Poisson capability with exact intervals in `attribute_capability`), acceptance sampling (single, double and k-method variables plans from risk points with OC, AOQ, ATI and ASN in `acceptance`), Gauge R&R (ANOVA-based), Pareto ranking with an "Other" pool (`pareto`), multi-vari breakdown by nested or crossed factors (`multivari`), multivariate charts (`multivariate`: Hotelling T², generalized variance |S|, MEWMA, with T² contributions); gauge study worksheets, bias/linearity, Cg/Cgk and intraclass correlation (`gauge_worksheet`, `gauge_bias`, `icc`).
- `crates/stat-reliability`: Kaplan-Meier, parametric Weibull/Lognormal survival fitting; reliability growth (Crow–AMSAA), repairable systems (mean cumulative function, trend tests) and reliability test plans.
- `crates/stat-predictive`: Coordinate-descent Elastic Net (Lasso/Ridge); CART classification and regression trees (surrogate splits, cost-complexity pruning, cross-validated size); random forests (bootstrap samples, random predictor subsets, out-of-bag error, permutation and impurity importance; grown in parallel with rayon, seeded per tree); gradient-boosted trees (squared, absolute, logistic and multinomial losses; histogram splits, Newton leaves with L2, subsampling, early stopping); partial least squares (NIPALS, SIMPLS, PLS-DA, VIP, factors by cross-validation); support vector machines (SMO with second-order working sets, linear/radial/polynomial kernels, one-against-one classes, Platt probabilities with pairwise coupling, grid tuning); multivariate adaptive regression splines (`mars`); neural networks with one or two hidden layers (`neural`); Gaussian-process regression (`gaussian_process`: Matérn 5/2 and squared-exponential kernels with one length scale per input, nugget, maximum likelihood from multi-start BFGS, exact leave-one-out) and next-run proposals (`acquisition`: expected improvement, target and desirability forms, upper confidence bound, constant-liar batches within constraints); validation roles (random, stratified, grouped, k-fold) and fit measures (RMSE, MAE, R², misclassification, log loss, AUC/ROC). The shared prediction framework (roles per row, fit by role, saved prediction columns) is `app_model::prediction`. Saved prediction columns are compared by `app_model::model_comparison`; the automated model search (`app_model::model_search`) fits every suitable model on the same validation roles. (Stepwise selection lives in `stat-linear`.)
- `crates/stat-bayes`: Bayesian analysis — conjugate posteriors with equal-tailed and HPD intervals, default Bayes factors (JZS t tests, correlation, contingency tables), g-prior linear models and ANOVA with model averaging, the No-U-Turn sampler with rank-normalized R̂/ESS/MCSE, PSIS-LOO and WAIC, and Bayesian GLMs with group effects. Verified against R BayesFactor, posterior and loo, and PyMC (`tests/data`). The reports are `app_model::bayes_analysis` and `app_model::bayes_models`.
- `crates/stat-functional`: Curves from long data — B-spline and Fourier bases with Gram and roughness-penalty matrices, penalized smoothing with GCV, landmark (PCHIP warps) and continuous (Ramsay–Li minimum-eigenvalue) registration, functional PCA. Verified against scikit-fda (`tests/data/reference_cases.py`). The report with score models and the Curve Explorer is `app_model::functional_analysis`.
- `crates/stat-text`: Text analysis — Unicode word segmentation, stop words, Porter stemming, phrases, document–term matrices with TF-IDF weightings, latent semantic analysis by truncated SVD (exact or randomized), LDA topic models by collapsed Gibbs sampling, and lexicon sentiment scores with negation (bundled VADER lexicon, MIT licence). Verified against Porter's reference output, NumPy, SciPy and vaderSentiment.
- `crates/stat-timeseries`: Equally spaced series — ACF/PACF, Ljung–Box, Yule–Walker AR, cross-correlation with prewhitening, differencing and Box–Cox (Guerrero λ), classical and STL decomposition, ADF and KPSS tests, trend models with accuracy measures, periodogram and smoothed spectrum, exponential smoothing in state-space form (all ETS forms, selection by AICc), seasonal ARIMA by exact Kalman-filter likelihood with forecasts and the stepwise automatic order search. Verified against R (stats, forecast, tseries, urca) and statsmodels.
- `crates/stat-signal`: Signals and spectra — Savitzky–Golay and other smoothing filters, x–y derivatives, cumulative trapezoid/Simpson integrals and linear, spline and PCHIP interpolation, baselines (asymmetric least squares, arPLS, SNIP), peak finding (height, prominence, separation), and multi-peak fitting (Gaussian, Lorentzian, pseudo-Voigt, Voigt via the Faddeeva function, split shapes) with standard errors and AICc/F comparison of peak counts; FFT of any length (mixed radix, Bluestein), windows, periodogram, Welch and spectrogram; IIR design in second-order sections (Butterworth, Chebyshev I/II, elliptic), windowed-sinc FIR, FFT and notch filters, forward or zero-phase; linear and circular convolution, cross- and autocorrelation, Wiener and Richardson–Lucy deconvolution, Hilbert envelope and phase; discrete wavelet transforms (haar, db, sym, coif) with SURE/universal denoising and the continuous wavelet transform. Verified against SciPy, NumPy, pandas, pybaselines, lmfit, PyWavelets and scikit-image (`tests/data/curves_reference_cases.py`, `tests/data/reference_cases.py`). The reports are `app_model::signal_curves` and `app_model::signal_analysis`.
- `crates/stat-viz`: Grammar-of-graphics graph engine — column-to-channel encodings (axes, panel splits, color, size, shape, subgroups), small-multiple panel layout and pages, axis scales (linear, log₁₀, ln, logit, square root, reciprocal), a per-graph row filter, frequency and weight columns, column switchers, and composable layers (jittered points; weighted polynomial fits with confidence and prediction bands, equation, R² and p-value; smoothing splines and LOESS with confidence bands; notched box plots and violins; summary statistics with error bars; density ellipses, kernel-density contours and hexagonal/square binning; formula curves; bars (side by side, stacked, 100%) with error bars, line and run charts, category heat maps; histograms, Wilkinson dot plots and probability plots against fitted distributions with order-statistic bands), plus treemap and parallel-coordinates chart forms; point labels and key placement; SVG/PDF/EPS export and a summary table. GUI-independent; an optional `egui` feature draws layers with `egui_plot`.
- `crates/stat-script`: Rhai scripting engine (tables, row states, table operations, analyses via `app_model::run_report`, report sections as data, file output; operation/size limits and cancellation) used by automation scripts, script notebooks (`NotebookSession`: cells sharing variables and functions) and replaying recorded actions; the `anovacraft-run` headless runner. (Formula columns use the same language through `app_model::formula`, which edits call, so it lives below this crate.) Script API reference: `docs/scripting.md`.
- `crates/stat-strd`: NIST StRD reference datasets with certified values, the StRD file parser, and the accuracy (log relative error) verification suite.
- `crates/app-model`: GUI-independent application logic — data edits with undo, formula columns (`formula`: per-row Rhai expressions recomputed after edits; reference `docs/formulas.md`), analysis runs bound to row state, report section content (formatted tables, plot data tagged with row indices), brushing gestures → `RowStateManager` updates. Fully unit tested; `app-gui` stays a thin rendering layer over it.
- `crates/app-gui`: `egui` desktop frontend featuring cross-chart brushing, collapsible hierarchical report trees, and interactive response explorers (see GUI Architecture & Interaction Model).

## Crate `app-gui` (`crates/app-gui`)

Desktop front end (egui/eframe): data grid, collapsible analysis reports and linked-brushing plots.

Dependencies: `app-model`, `chrono`, `eframe`, `egui_extras`, `egui_plot`, `resvg`, `stat-bayes`, `stat-core`, `stat-data`, `stat-doe`, `stat-predictive`, `stat-quality`, `stat-script`, `stat-signal`, `stat-viz`.

### `crates/app-gui/src/agreement_dialog.rs`

Dialogs for the attribute measurement studies: the attribute agreement
study of appraisers' categorical ratings and the go/no-go gauge study of
bias and repeatability ([`app_model::attribute_agreement`]).

Both reports run through [`app_model::ComparisonReport`], so their
settings are also edited in place from the report's options menu
([`report_settings`]).

- `enum AgreementTool`: Which study the dialog sets up.
- `struct AgreementDialog`: Dialog for the attribute studies.
- `fn report_settings`: In-report settings of the reports this module sets up; `false` for any other report.

### `crates/app-gui/src/anom_dialog.rs`

Dialog for an analysis of means (means, proportions or rates; one- or
two-way for means).

- `struct AnomDialog`

### `crates/app-gui/src/app/crash.rs`

Panics: the crash-report hook, and running an analysis so that a panic
inside it becomes that report's error instead of closing the program.

The reports and recovery folders are described in
[`app_model::recovery`].

- `fn crashed`: Whether the program is ending in a panic (so the recovery copies must be kept for the next launch).
- `fn set_session_dir`: Tell the hook which folder holds this run's recovery copies.
- `fn panic_text`: The text of a panic payload.
- `fn guarded`: Run `f`, turning a panic into `Err` with a message for the report.
- `fn install_panic_hook`: Install the hook that writes a crash report for every panic (marked as caught for panics inside [`guarded`]) before the standard message.

### `crates/app-gui/src/app/dashboards.rs`

Dashboards: reports and notes from a project's tables arranged on a grid,
with local filters shared by every tile (roadmap §10; the engine is
[`app_model::dashboard`]).

A dashboard belongs to an open project and uses only that project's
tables. It is listed under the project in the sidebar and has a tab after
the project's tables; showing it fills the main window's workspace (or a
window of its own) with:

* a toolbar: the dashboard's name, Undo and Redo of dashboard edits, "Add
  tile" (a copy of a report of one of the project's tables, a graph
  canvas, a heading or a note), "Export as HTML…" and "New window";
* the filter strip: one condition per column name, offered for every
  column of the project's tables, with the graph canvas's level and range
  choices. A filter applies to each tile whose table has that column; a
  tile whose table lacks it says so in its strip. Filters never change
  the tables' own row states: each tile runs on a copy with the rows
  outside the filters excluded and hidden, and its report says how many
  rows were "filtered out" (rather than "excluded");
* the switcher strip: shared column pickers, one per column name. A
  switcher steps through its choices (previous, list, next); every report
  tile that reads its column shows the chosen column in its place, and a
  tile it cannot switch (its table lacks the column, or it already reads
  it) says so in its strip. Tiles keep their own requests: a display
  option changed in a switched tile is stored against the switcher's own
  column ([`Dashboard::unswitched_report`]);
* the grid: tiles on the engine's 12 columns, each moved by dragging its
  strip, resized by dragging its corner, and removed with its ×.

A tile holds its own copy of a report request bound to one table (made by
the report's "Add to dashboard" or by "Add tile"); changing the tile's
display options changes that copy only. Selecting rows in a tile selects
them in its table (so in that table's grid and every other view of it),
never in other tables. Every change to the dashboard (adding, moving,
resizing and removing tiles, filters, switchers, display options, its name) is one
[`DashboardEdit`] in the dashboard's [`DashboardHistory`], so Undo and
Redo work. Dashboards, their windows and the dashboard shown are saved in
the project file.

### `crates/app-gui/src/app/folders.rs`

Folders in a project's tree in the sidebar.

A project's tree lists its tables (each with its reports and graph
canvases under it), dashboards and notebooks. The user can add folders
(right-click ▸ New folder, or Move to folder ▸ New folder on an item),
rename them in place, nest them, and move items into them by dragging an
item onto a folder (or onto the project's name to take it out of every
folder) or with right-click ▸ Move to folder. A folder only groups: a
report in a folder still belongs to its table.

Clicking a folder's name brings the windows of everything in it to the
front; when none of it is in a window, the main window shows its first
table or dashboard. Right-click ▸ Open each in a window gives every item
a window of its own.

Folders are saved with the project ([`app_model::project::ProjectFolder`]):
here items are held by their ids for this session (documents, reports and
dashboards keep their ids however they move), and turned into the file's
table ids and report positions when the project is saved.

### `crates/app-gui/src/app/manuals.rs`

The two manuals the app carries as PDFs (built from `docs/guide` and
`docs/manual` by `scripts/build-manual-pdfs.sh`): Help ▸ Quick guide and
Help ▸ Reference manual write the embedded PDF to the app's data folder
and open it in the system's PDF viewer, so they work offline and show the
books rather than their Markdown sources.

### `crates/app-gui/src/app/notebooks.rs`

Script notebooks kept in projects (Scripts ▸ New notebook, Scripts ▸
Notebooks): the windows, running their cells on the open documents and
merging what the cells did.

### `crates/app-gui/src/app/notes.rs`

Project notes: free text kept with each project and saved in its file.

The sidebar shows the notes of the project the menus act on (the active
document's), below the row counts, so working in another project's table
switches to that project's notes. The notes can move into a window of
their own, which follows the active project in the same way; closing it
(or "Back to sidebar") puts them back in the sidebar.

### `crates/app-gui/src/app/notices.rs`

Help ▸ About ▸ Open-source licences: the copyright notices and licence
texts of the fonts, icons, data and Rust crates built into the app.

The text is `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt` at the repository root, written by
`scripts/build-notices.py` from Cargo.lock and the crates' own licence
files, and embedded so it travels with the executable.

### `crates/app-gui/src/app/projects.rs`

Open projects: one project file holds one or more tables.

Every open table (a [`Document`]) belongs to an [`OpenProject`], which
holds what the file holds besides the tables: its path, its scripts and
whether it has unsaved changes. A project with one table looks and works
as a single dataset always has; a project with several is listed in the
sidebar as a tree (the project, its tables, and tables made from another
table indented under it) and its bottom tabs sit together after the
project's name.

Tables made by Data ▸ Rows, Reshape, Merge or Summarize, augmented
designs and tables saved from reports join the project of the table they
came from unless the dialog's "Keep in this project" box is cleared. A
table made by a table operation keeps its lineage: the operation, and the
id and a fingerprint of each source in the project
([`app_model::project::TableLineage`]). When a source's data no longer
matches its fingerprint, the derived table is marked (⚠ in the sidebar
and its tab, a banner above its grid) and offers Update, which runs the
operation again ([`ProjectFile::rerun_origin`]) and puts the result in
the table as one undoable edit. Nothing is updated without being asked.

Saving writes the whole project ([`app_model::project::save_project_file`]),
with its layout: the table shown, each table's view and the windows of
their own with their places. A project of one table with nothing to
record in its layout is still written in the one-table form older
builds read.

### `crates/app-gui/src/app/recovery.rs`

Recovery saves while the program runs, and the offer to restore them
after a run that ended abnormally (see [`app_model::recovery`]).

Every [`SAVE_INTERVAL`] seconds the app hands a copy of each open
project to a writer thread, which serializes it and writes it to this
run's recovery folder if it changed since it was opened or saved. Copying
the tables is the only work on the drawing thread.

### `crates/app-gui/src/app/renaming.rs`

Renaming tables, projects and folders in place: in the sidebar's list of open
projects and in the tabs along the bottom edge, a double-click or
right-click ▸ Rename turns the name into a text box. Enter (or clicking
elsewhere) keeps the new name, Escape keeps the old one.

### `crates/app-gui/src/app/reuse.rs`

Reusing plots and reports elsewhere: pasting a copied plot style,
"Duplicate on another table…" and project templates (File ▸ Save
project as template…, File ▸ New project from template…).

The work is done by `app_model::style_paste`,
`app_model::report_transfer` and `app_model::project_template`; this
module holds the dialogs, which ask for the target table (or data files)
and for the column standing in for each column whose name differs.

### `crates/app-gui/src/app/row_styles.rs`

Row colours and markers from a column (Data ▸ Row states ▸ Colour and
marker by column…): every row takes a colour, and for a categorical
column a marker, from its value, and every plot without a grouping of
its own draws them (`stat_viz::row_styles`).

### `crates/app-gui/src/app/subsets.rs`

Saved row subsets (Data ▸ Row subsets, and the sidebar's Rows section):
named sets of rows a table keeps, one of which can be active so that
every report, plot and summary uses only its rows.

### `crates/app-gui/src/app/viewer.rs`

The read-only dashboard viewer: a published project's dashboards shown
full window, with no menus, sidebar or tabs. This is what the web build
runs (`web_main`); it is a mode of [`StatsApp`] so the viewer draws the
very same tiles, reports and plots as the desktop app.

Filters, column pickers, brushing and display options work as in the
app, recomputed in place; tiles cannot be added, moved, resized, removed
or edited, nothing creates columns, reports or tables, and nothing is
saved.

- `fn publish_sample`: Publish the Greenhouse sample project's dashboard to `folder` (created if missing), as "Publish dashboard as web app…" would: what `scripts/build-web-viewer.sh --serve` shows.

### `crates/app-gui/src/app/viewer_build.rs`

"Publish as web app…" needs the web viewer (the app built for
WebAssembly, `scripts/build-web-viewer.sh`), which an ordinary
`cargo run` does not make. When it is missing, Publish writes nothing
and this window says so, shows the command that builds it and, in a
source checkout, builds it in the background and then carries on with
the publish.

### `crates/app-gui/src/app/welcome.rs`

The start page, shown whenever no table is open (including at startup):
ways to start a table beside the recent projects, a grid of common tasks,
and the sample data, the user manual and a tip.

A task that needs data, chosen with no table open, brings up a small
"Open data for …" dialog in front ([`StatsApp::task_data_dialog`]) while
it waits ([`StatsApp::pending_task`]); the task's dialog opens once a table
is opened from there. Cancelling, or opening data some other way, drops
the task, so nothing waits out of sight.

### `crates/app-gui/src/app/windows.rs`

Views in windows of their own.

A document's data grid, its results pane, or a single report can be
shown in a native window of its own (an egui *immediate* viewport, drawn
from the same application state during the main window's frame, so a
selection made in one window shows in every other window on the same
frame). A view lives in exactly one place: while it has a window, the
main window shows a panel saying so, with buttons to bring the window to
the front or the view back.

Closing such a window (its close button, ⌘W / Ctrl+W in it, or its "Back
to main window" button) puts the view back in the main window; nothing
is closed. Closing the document closes its windows.

The document a window belongs to becomes the command target (the one the
menus, dialogs and the sidebar act on) when the window is used, without
changing what the main window shows. Shortcuts pressed in a window act
on that window's document.

When egui draws viewports inside the main window instead (as the headless
tests do), each view's window is an ordinary egui window drawn by the
same code.

### `crates/app-gui/src/app.rs`

Top-level application state and frame layout.

The application holds any number of open documents — a dataset with its row
states and reports — one of which is active. Open documents are listed as
tabs along the bottom of the window and in the left sidebar, where
right-clicking an entry offers save, export and close. Opening a file or a
sample while a document is open adds a new document rather than replacing it.

A document's data grid, its results pane or a single report can also be
shown in a native window of its own ([`windows`]). The main window then
shows one document (`shown`) while menus, dialogs and the sidebar act on
the document of the window used last (`active`, the command target).

A project can also hold dashboards ([`dashboards`]): tiles of reports and
notes from its tables on a grid, with shared filters. The main window
shows either a table or one of its project's dashboards
(`shown_dashboard`), and a dashboard can have a window of its own.

- `struct StatsApp`

### `crates/app-gui/src/attribute_dialog.rs`

Dialog for a count chart: p, np, c, u, Laney p′ and u′, and the
rare-event g and t charts, with an optional phase column and run rules.

- `struct AttributeDialog`

### `crates/app-gui/src/augment_dialog.rs`

Dialog for augmenting the design held in the active table: choose the
factor and response columns and a method (fold-over, center runs, axial
runs, D-optimal runs or new whole plots of a split-plot design); the preview shows how many runs are added and
the notes, and Create opens the augmented design as a new document
([`app_model::design_augment`]).

- `const TITLE`: The dialog's title.
- `struct AugmentDialog`

### `crates/app-gui/src/axis_drop.rs`

Dropping a column on a report plot's axis: when the axis shows the
report's switchable column (a model's response, a distribution's or a
chart's column; see [`app_model::SavedReport::axis_drop`]), a column
dragged from the variables list highlights the axis and, let go there,
re-runs the report with that column in its place, as the column
switcher would.

While a report is drawn its drop target sits in the context's temporary
data, where the shared axis code ([`axis_drop_zone`]) finds it; a drop
is left there for the report to take after drawing.

- `fn begin`: Make `report` the target of axis drops while it is drawn (only while a column is being dragged, so nothing is computed otherwise).
- `fn end`: Stop taking axis drops for the report drawn, and return the column dropped on one of its axes, if any.
- `fn axis_drop_zone`: The drop zone of one axis: its ruler `strip`, which shows the column named `title`.

### `crates/app-gui/src/batch_window.rs`

Scripts ▸ Run script over a folder: run one script once per data file in
a folder (see `stat_script::batch`) on a background thread, show its
output as it comes, and open what the runs returned as a new table.

- `struct BatchWindow`: The batch window's state.
- `type WindowScript`: The script in the Script window: text, name, folder for relative paths.

### `crates/app-gui/src/bayes_dialog.rs`

Dialogs for the Bayesian analyses (Compare ▸ Bayesian and Model ▸
Bayesian): estimation of a mean, proportion or rate with conjugate
priors, Bayes factor tests, the Bayesian linear model or ANOVA, and the
Bayesian regression or hierarchical model sampled by NUTS
([`app_model::bayes_analysis`], [`app_model::bayes_models`]).

Every report runs through [`app_model::ComparisonReport`], so its
settings are also edited in place from the report's options menu
([`report_settings`]).

- `enum BayesTool`: Which Bayesian analysis the dialog sets up.
- `const MENU`: The menu entries of the Bayesian submenu: label, hover text and tool.
- `struct BayesDialog`: Dialog for the Bayesian analyses.
- `fn report_settings`: In-report settings of a Bayesian report; `labels` are the report's parameter names (for the parameter shown in the sampler plots).

### `crates/app-gui/src/boost_dialog.rs`

Dialog for gradient-boosted trees: response, predictors, validation (which
chooses the number of rounds), and the boosting settings.

- `struct BoostDialog`

### `crates/app-gui/src/capability_dialog.rs`

Dialog for a process capability study, optionally laid out as a summary
page with bootstrap intervals for the non-normal indices.

- `struct CapabilityDialog`
- `fn report_options`: In-report options of a capability study added by the by column and the probability plot.

### `crates/app-gui/src/chart_dialog.rs`

The control chart dialog: a chart built from column roles.

Each role takes a column chosen from its list or dragged from the
variables list: the measurement, an optional subgroup ID (rows sharing a

part number for short-run charts. The chart type can be changed here or
later from the report's options menu.

### `crates/app-gui/src/dialog_kit.rs`

Parts every dialog shares, so they look and behave alike:

- a window that opens centred, can be moved and resized, and reopens where
  it was left ([`Dialog`]);
- the action row at its foot: **Run** for analyses or **Create** for
  designs and tables (**Update** and **Run as new** when editing an
  existing report), **Cancel**, and **Reset**, with a one-line summary of
  what the action will do and the rows it will use, or a note saying what
  is missing while the action is unavailable;
- keys: Enter runs (⌘/Ctrl+Enter while typing in a field), Escape cancels;
- a collapsed "More options" section for settings most people leave alone
  ([`more_options`]);
- column pickers with a filter box, measurement-level badges, Select all /
  none, Shift-click ranges and drops from the sidebar's variable list
  ([`column_list`], [`column_choice`]);
- for analyses, a **Script** toggle that shows the Rhai call the dialog
  would run, built live from its settings, with a button to copy it.

- `enum Verb`: The main action's verb: analyses run, designs and tables are created.
- `enum Placement`: Where a dialog's new report goes.
- `enum Outcome`: What happened in a dialog this frame.
- `struct Ready`: A dialog ready to run: what it would produce, and a short sentence saying what that is ("Linear model of Yield on 3 effects").
- `type Readiness`: The dialog's state this frame: ready, or what is missing.
- `fn ready`: Shorthand for a ready dialog.
- `struct RowCounts`: Rows of the active table, shown in each analysis dialog's summary.
- `fn set_column_names`: Record the active table's column names for this frame's dialogs.
- `fn set_row_counts`: Record the active table's row counts for this frame's dialogs.
- `fn set_project_name`: Tell this frame's dialogs which project the active table belongs to.
- `fn project_name`: The active table's project name, as the app set it this frame.
- `fn keep_in_project`: The "Keep in this project (name)" check box of dialogs that make a new table: ticked, the table joins the project of the table it came from; cleared, it opens as a separate document.
- `fn rows_note`: "48 rows" or "46 of 48 rows (2 excluded)".
- `fn em`: The text height, for widths that grow with the text-size setting.
- `fn seed_value`: A number field for a random seed.
- `fn combo_width`: Width of a drop-down list of column names.
- `struct Dialog`: A dialog window with the shared action row.
- `fn more_options`: Settings most people leave alone, in a section that starts closed.
- `fn overflow_cues`: Cues that a scrolled list has more entries than it shows: call it last inside a vertical scroll area's contents.
- `trait ComboExt`: [`egui::ComboBox::show_ui`] with [`overflow_cues`] on its list, so a long drop-down list shows that it scrolls.
- `fn note`: A faint explanatory line.
- `fn level`: The level of column `i`, or continuous for a missing column.
- `fn is_continuous`: Whether column `i` is numeric and continuous.
- `fn is_numeric`: Whether column `i` is numeric (any level).
- `fn name`: Column `i`'s name ("" if there is none).
- `fn column_list`: A list of check boxes, one per column `allow`ed, for choosing several columns: a filter box (when the list is long), each column's level badge, Select all / Select none, Shift-click to set a whole range like the clicked box, and columns dragged from the sidebar's variable list are added.
- `fn column_choice`: A drop-down list for choosing one column among those `allow`ed: each entry shows the column's level badge, long lists get a filter box, and a column dragged from the sidebar's variable list onto it is chosen.
- `fn all_different`: Whether `columns` are all different (ignoring unset roles).
- `fn duplicate_role`: The message for the first column given two roles in `roles` (role name, chosen column), naming the column and both roles; `None` when every set role has its own column.
- `fn count`: "1 column" / "3 columns".
- `fn chosen_columns`: Columns `chosen` (by index), in table order.
- `fn mask`: A `Vec<bool>` per column with `columns` set.
- `fn valid`: A column index from a saved request, kept only if the table has it.
- `struct Memory`: Remembered dialog settings, per document and dialog, while the app runs (B2).
- `trait Remember`: A dialog whose settings can be remembered, restored, reset, pre-filled and pointed at a report to edit.

### `crates/app-gui/src/figure_page_window.rs`

Visualize ▸ Figure page…: several plots on one page with panel letters,

[`stat_viz::figure_page`]).

Plots join the page from their right-click menus ("Add to figure page",
next to the "Save plot as" items, and on the graph canvas's output
menu). Report plots and graph canvases are kept as a copy of what they
show, redrawn at the size of their cell whenever the page changes, so
their text keeps its point size; other pictures (3-D views, trees,
diagrams, word clouds) are kept as they were drawn and shrunk to fit.
The page lasts while the app is open.

The window holds the page settings (size in millimetres or inches, with
journal-column and paper presets; columns; space between panels; a
title; the letter style and size; whether plots keep their own titles),
the list of panels (each with its letter, the columns it spans, and
buttons to move or remove it), a preview, and the file settings: format,
pixel density for PNG, CMYK colour for PDF and EPS, the font (sans serif
or serif), and a transparent background.

### `crates/app-gui/src/filter_panel.rs`

The filter panel: a form for a row filter's conditions (a level list per
categorical column, "from" and "to" sliders per continuous one) with
stepping through levels. Reports and graph canvases share it.

Stepping shows one level of a condition's column at a time (for a
continuous column, a window of fixed width moved along it), by hand with
Previous and Next or automatically with Play, at a chosen number of
seconds per step. It is the conditioning-plot idea of Cleveland
(*Visualizing Data*, 1993) put in time: the same view drawn for each
slice of a conditioning variable in turn.

- `struct FilterPanelState`: On-screen state of one filter panel (not saved).
- `fn filter_panel`: The panel's contents: one block per condition (its column, Step through, ×, then its levels or sliders, and the stepping controls while stepping) and "+ Add condition".
- `fn data_range`: Smallest and largest finite value of a numeric column (`(0, 1)` without any; a single value is widened to one unit).

### `crates/app-gui/src/graph_view.rs`

The graph canvas: column shelves that assign data columns to visual
channels, a layer bar that switches drawing elements on and off, and a grid
of linked panels (small multiples) drawn from [`stat_viz`].

Every panel follows the application's plot interaction model: no scroll
zoom; each axis is a draggable ruler (ends rescale, middle shifts); dragging
inside a panel selects the rows under the box in the shared row state, so
the data grid and every other plot highlight them at once. Panels showing
the same column share that axis's range, so moving one axis moves it in
every panel. Statistics labels (fit equations and R², ellipse
correlations) are the one exception to box selection: dragging one moves it.
Columns on the right-axis shelf are drawn against a second scale on the
right of each panel, whose ruler drags like the left one; an axis break
set in Plot settings leaves a stretch out of an axis.

While a column is dragged, drop zones over the panels (edges for the
axes and splits, centre for colour) take it as the shelves would; the
row filter can sit in a panel beside the graph, with stepping through
levels.

The shelf design follows the shelf-based view specification of Stolte,
Tang & Hanrahan ("Polaris", *IEEE TVCG* 8(1), 2002) and the panel grid the
trellis displays of Becker, Cleveland & Shyu (*JCGS* 5(2), 1996); labels
and layout are this application's own.

- `struct ColumnDrag`: A column being dragged from the variables list or from another shelf.

### `crates/app-gui/src/heat_map_view.rs`

A heat map section (for example a correlation matrix), painted as a grid

for the sign, contrast with the neutral for the size), and its value is
printed in it, so the colour is never the only cue. A key under the grid
shows the ramp with its end values; hovering a cell names its row and
column.

### `crates/app-gui/src/macos_open.rs`

macOS: receive files opened from Finder (double-click, Open With, or
dropping them on the Dock icon).

macOS asks the application to open documents with an "open documents"
Apple Event (`'aevt'`/`'odoc'`). The window library does not handle it, so
AppKit's default handler answered "cannot open files of this type". This
module installs its own handler with the Apple Event Manager C API, at the
moment Apple documents for doing so — when the application posts
`NSApplicationWillFinishLaunchingNotification`, after AppKit has installed
its default handlers and before the launch event is dispatched — observed
through the CoreFoundation notification centre (the same centre as
`NSNotificationCenter`'s default centre). The handler only records the
files' paths; the app opens them on its next frame through the ordinary
open path.

#### Safety
This is the only module in the workspace that uses `unsafe`: plain C calls
into CoreFoundation and the Apple Event Manager (part of CoreServices),
with the types and constants of their public headers. Every pointer passed
in is either a valid local, a `'static` C string, or one handed to us by
the system for the duration of the callback; every descriptor obtained is
disposed of; nothing is retained across calls except plain Rust data
behind a mutex.

- `fn install`: Arrange to receive open-document requests.
- `fn set_context`: Remember the UI context so arriving files wake the app, and make sure the handler is installed (a no-op repeat if launch already installed it).
- `fn take_pending`: Files received since the last call.

### `crates/app-gui/src/main.rs`

AnovaCraft desktop application.

Run with `cargo run -p app-gui` to open the built-in sample dataset, or
`cargo run -p app-gui -- file1.csv file2.acraft …` to open files, each in
its own tab. Data files (CSV, TSV, delimited text, JSON, Excel and
OpenDocument spreadsheets) and project files can also be opened from the
File menu or dropped onto the window.

All application logic (analyses, report content, brushing) lives in the
`app-model` crate; this crate only draws it and forwards user input.

### `crates/app-gui/src/menus.rs`

Drop-down menu buttons that toggle: clicking the button of an open menu
closes it, without the menu flashing back for a frame.

egui's own menu button closes the menu when a press lands outside the
menu's area (the button is outside it) and then, seeing a click on the
button of a closed menu, reopens it on the release. This wrapper remembers
the open menu when a press on its button begins, and puts it back just before
the release is handled, so egui sees "button of the open menu clicked" and
closes it, never drawing it again.

- `fn menu_button`: A top-level drop-down menu (in the menu bar or a toolbar row).

### `crates/app-gui/src/plot_clipboard.rs`

Copy plot: one figure on the system clipboard in several formats at
once, so each program pastes the best one it reads.

* macOS: PNG (`public.png`), PDF (`com.adobe.pdf`, which Keynote, Pages,
  Word and PowerPoint paste as a vector picture) and SVG
  (`public.svg-image`).
* Windows: a device-independent bitmap (the format most programs
  paste), PNG (the registered `PNG` format Office reads) and SVG
  (`image/svg+xml`). Windows programs paste vector pictures as EMF,
  which is not written, so the picture pastes as a bitmap there.
* Linux (X11): `image/png`, `application/pdf` and `image/svg+xml`.

When the clipboard refuses the set, the PNG alone is tried before giving
up, and the outcome says which formats went on.

### `crates/app-gui/src/plot_export.rs`

A plot's figure output: the Copy plot and Save plot as… items of its
right-click menu, the Save plot dialog (size on paper, resolution,
background, font and text size, with a preview), the Transparent
background and Plot font items, and the figure look they share
([`ExportLook`], kept in the plot's style).

A plot's look is kept by its owner: report plots in their report's plot
styles, graph canvases in their graph. Menus and the dialog post a
changed look under the plot's [`target`]; the owner takes it on its next
frame ([`take_change`]). Pictures that keep no style (3-D views, trees,
diagrams, word clouds) keep their look for the session
([`session_look`]).

Figures drawn with the default look are written exactly as before; any
other look redraws the plot at its size on paper (or its on-screen size)
and writes it through [`stat_viz::figure_page::look_figure`].

### `crates/app-gui/src/plot_size.rs`

The size of a plot and the grip that changes it.

Every plot in a report opens at a default size and can be resized by
dragging: a strip under it changes the height, a strip along its right
edge changes the width, and the corner where they meet changes both.
Double-clicking either restores the default. The width never exceeds the
visible part of the pane, so the whole plot stays in view.

A row of small plots (the panels of a Response Explorer) shares one grip:
dragging it resizes every panel together, by the same amount, so the
grabbed corner follows the pointer whatever the number of panels.

"Copy plot style" and "Paste plot style" in plot menus.

The copied style is kept for the session in the context's data, so any
plot in any window can take it. A paste is a request a report hands to
the app ([`StyleRequest`]), which carries it out on the report, or on
every report of the project (see `app_model::style_paste`).

- `enum PasteTarget`: Where a pasted style goes.
- `enum StyleRequest`: What a report's plot menu asked for (taken by the app).
- `fn copied`: The copied style, if any.
- `fn set_copied`: Keep `style` as the copied style.
- `fn parts`: The parts a paste carries (ticked in the paste menu).
- `fn menu_items`: "Copy plot style" and the "Paste plot style" submenu for a plot with style key `key` (`None`: a graph canvas), writing what was chosen into `request`.
- `fn canvas_menu_items`: [`menu_items`] for the graph canvas of report `report`; the request is kept until the report takes it ([`take_canvas_request`]).
- `fn take_canvas_request`: A request made in the canvas menu of report `report`.

A report's own row filter strip and column picker bar (see

The filter strip sits under a report's title line: one chip per

### `crates/app-gui/src/report_view/jobs.rs`

Reports computed on background threads, so that editing data, excluding
rows or changing a report's filter never waits for a slow analysis.

A report that needs computing again hands a [`Job`] to [`ReportJobs`]:
its request, display options and scope ([`JobKey`]), with snapshots of
the table (shared, see `Document::table`) and the row states. A worker
builds a fresh report body and its sections; the app installs the result
on the next frame ([`super::Report::install`]) if the report still wants
what was computed, and otherwise queues it again. Each report has at most
one job running, so a burst of edits costs at most two computations.

- `struct Done`: A finished job: the report it is for, which of its jobs, what it was computed from, and the result (or why the analysis stopped).
- `struct ReportJobs`: The background workers and the queue between them and the app.

Plots do not move with scrolling. Each axis is draggable: near either end a

([`app_model::plot_view`]). Every plot has a "Reset view" button, the report
options menu a "Reset all plot views" item, and double-clicking a plot also

- `fn show_plot_hint_id`: Where the app puts the getting-started tips setting, which also shows the plot hint line above the reports.

- `fn show_reports`: The reports pane: a toolbar (collapse, expand, export, go to) above every report, newest first.
- `fn show_single_report`: One report in a window of its own: the report in a scroll area that fills the window, its plots sized to the window.

### `crates/app-gui/src/response_explorer.rs`

The Response Explorer of a fitted linear model: one panel per factor showing
the predicted response (with its confidence band) as that factor varies and
every other factor stays at its current setting.

Each continuous panel has a vertical line at the factor's setting; dragging
or clicking in the panel moves it, and every panel and the predicted value
update at once. Categorical panels show the prediction at each level with its
confidence interval; clicking a level selects it. Exact values can be typed
below each panel. All panels share one vertical scale, so the size of each
factor's effect can be compared directly. The panels do not pan or zoom.

One grip under the panels resizes them all together (the strip changes
every panel's height, its corner and the strip beside the last panel the
width); double-clicking it restores the default size. The size is kept for
each report while the application runs.

Any fitted model implementing [`app_model::SurfaceModel`] can be explored:
linear models, response surfaces, logistic and Poisson models, penalized
fits (no bands) and mixtures (moving one component rescales the others).
The model logic (predictions, intervals, ranges) is
[`app_model::surface_profiler::profile`]; this module only draws it.

- `fn show`: Draw the explorer for `analysis`, reading and updating `settings` (one value per model term; reset to the defaults when they no longer fit).
- `fn linked`: The linked explorer of several responses over the same factors: one row of panels per profile (each on its own vertical scale), every row at the same settings, so moving a factor in any row moves it in all of them.

### `crates/app-gui/src/scatter3d_view.rs`

The 3-D scatter plot: rows placed by three columns in a box that turns
and tilts as the plot is dragged, with colour, size and marker-shape
channels, optional drop lines to the floor, and linked brushing.

Points are painted back to front (the painter's algorithm), each with a
thin outline in the contrasting ink so overlapping points stay apart.
Grouped colours always come with a distinct marker shape (or the shape
column's shapes, with every colour named in the key), and a continuous
colour column has a labelled colour bar, so colour is never the only cue.
Excluded rows are drawn hollow; hidden rows are left out.

The rows, ranges and channels come from [`app_model::Scatter3dAnalysis`];
the projection is [`app_model::Camera`]; the box, axes and figure files
are shared with the 3-D surface views ([`crate::surface_profiler`]).

- `struct Scatter3dView`: Interaction state of one 3-D scatter plot (its angle and drop lines are display options saved with the project).
- `fn show`: Draw the plot and its controls, updating `options` (angle, drop lines) and the shared row state.

### `crates/app-gui/src/script_edit.rs`

Editing aids for the Script window and script notebook cells: folding of
`{ … }` blocks, bracket matching, completion of script functions and
column names, and find and replace. Plain text logic, so it is tested
without a window.

Positions are byte offsets into the text (always on character
boundaries) unless a name says otherwise.

- `const FOLD_MARK`: What a folded block shows in its place.
- `struct Block`: A `{ … }` block spanning several lines: `open` and `close` are the byte offsets of its braces, `line` the 0-based line of the opening brace.
- `fn foldable_blocks`: Blocks of `text` that span more than one line, by their opening brace's position.
- `struct Folding`: A text with some blocks folded: the editor shows and edits [`Self::shown`], in which each folded block's inside is replaced by [`FOLD_MARK`]; the full text is [`Self::full`].
- `fn bracket_pairs`: Pairs of matching brackets (`()`, `[]`, `{}`) outside strings and comments, as byte offsets of the opening and closing bracket.
- `fn matching_bracket`: The bracket next to the cursor (at byte `cursor`: the one just before it, else the one just after) and its partner, as byte offsets; `None` when the cursor is not beside a matched bracket.
- `struct Typed`: What is being typed at the cursor.
- `fn typed_at`: The word, or the start of a string literal's text, ending at byte `cursor`.
- `fn declared_names`: Names declared in the script with `let`, `const` or `fn`.
- `struct Candidate`: One completion offered.
- `fn candidates`: Completions of `typed`: column names inside a string, otherwise script functions (with their shortest signature) and names the script declares.
- `struct FindOptions`: How to match in find and replace.
- `fn find_all`: Byte ranges of the matches of `needle` in `text`, without overlaps.
- `fn replace_all`: `text` with every match replaced, and how many there were.
- `fn char_index`: Character index of byte offset `byte` in `text`.
- `fn byte_index`: Byte offset of character index `chars` in `text` (the end if beyond).

The sidebar's script library: the `.rhai` files in the scripts folder
(chosen once, kept in the settings) and the scripts kept in the active
project. Clicking a script opens it in the Script window; right-click
runs it, or keeps a folder script in the project.

- `enum LibraryOp`: What to do with a script file of the library.
- `enum LibraryRequest`: What the section asks the application to do.
- `enum ProjectRequest`: What to do with a script kept in the active project.
- `struct ScriptLibrary`: The listed folder, cached between frames.

### `crates/app-gui/src/script_window.rs`

The Script window: edit, open, save and run Rhai scripts against the open
documents (see `stat_script` and `docs/scripting.md`).

A run happens on a background thread, on copies of the open documents,
so the window stays responsive and Stop works between operations. When
it ends, the application merges what the script did (see
`StatsApp::apply_script_run`): data edits become one undoable step,
reports follow their columns, and tables the script showed open as new
documents.

- `const RUN_SHORTCUT`: Run the whole script.
- `enum ScriptEvent`: What the window asks the application to do.

### `crates/app-gui/src/surface_profiler.rs`

The 3-D surface profiler: a shaded, rotatable surface of a fitted model's
predicted response over two continuous factors, with contour lines drawn
on the surface, a contour map on the floor of the box, and the current
setting marked. The other factors are held at settings chosen above the
plot (shared with the Response Explorer for linear models).

Height is shown three ways — position against the vertical axis, contour
lines with a labelled legend, and a sequential colour ramp — so colour is
never the only cue. Dragging the plot turns and tilts the view (there are
no data points to select in this view); double-click or "Reset view"
restores the default angle. The view never responds to scrolling.

The grid, contours, projection and painting order come from
[`app_model::surface_profiler`]; this module only draws them.

- `struct SurfaceProfilerState`: View and display settings of one surface profiler (not saved with the project).
- `fn show`: Draw the profiler for `model`, reading and updating `settings` (one value per factor; reset to the model's defaults when they no longer fit).

The 3-D view of a contour and surface plot of data: the surface made
through the observations, shaded or as a wireframe, with contour lines on
it and on the floor, and the observations as points that can be selected.

The grid and its contours come from [`app_model::DataSurfaceAnalysis::mesh`];
drawing, rotation, brushing and figure files are shared with the 3-D
surface profiler ([`crate::surface_profiler::plot`]). The view's settings
are display options of the report, saved with the project.

Dialogs for the Data menu's table operations (Rows, Reshape, Merge and

### `crates/app-gui/src/table_view.rs`

Editable, virtualized data grid. Only the rows in view are laid out each
frame (`egui_extras::TableBody::rows`), so large tables stay responsive.

Editing works like a spreadsheet: a click puts the cell cursor on a cell;
double-click, Enter or F2 — or simply typing — edits it; Enter / Tab
commit and move down / right (Shift reverses), Escape cancels. Arrow keys
move the cursor (with ⌘/Ctrl to the edge of the table; Home / End, Page
Up / Down too); Shift with any of them, Shift-click or dragging across
cells makes a block of cells; ⌘A / Ctrl+A selects every cell. Delete
clears the block, ⌘D / Ctrl+D fills its first row down. Copy (⌘C /
Ctrl+C) puts the selected columns, the block, the selected rows (two or
more) or the cursor cell on the clipboard as tab-separated text; Cut also
clears them; Paste (⌘V / Ctrl+V) stores clipboard text with its top-left
value at the block's corner or the cursor (see [`app_model::clipboard`]).

Selecting: a click on a column heading selects the column, Shift-click
the run of columns from the last one clicked, ⌘/Ctrl-click adds or
removes one, and dragging across headings selects a run. Row numbers do
the same for rows, and their selection is the shared row selection that
every plot highlights ([`app_model::brushing::row_number_click`]). A click
in a data cell only moves the cursor.

Right-click a column heading for rename, sorting, type, level, insert and
delete; right-click a row number to select, exclude / include, hide / show,
insert or delete rows.

The grid never changes the data itself: it returns [`GridRequest`]s that
the application applies through the undo history.

- `enum GridRequest`: A change the user asked for in the grid.
- `struct GridState`: Cell cursor and in-progress edits for one dataset's grid.
- `fn show`: Draw the toolbar and grid; return the edits the user asked for.
- `fn level_badge`: The measurement level as a small coloured badge holding the level's icon, drawn from the Lucide icon set (ISC licence, `assets/icons/LICENSE-Lucide.txt`): `ruler` for continuous, `tag` for nominal and `list-ordered` for ordinal columns.
- `fn column_menu`: The right-click menu of column heading `j` (also shown for the variable in the sidebar).
- `const ROWS_KEY`: Session memory of the "How many" field of the row insert actions.
- `const COLUMNS_KEY`: Session memory of the "How many" field of the column insert actions.
- `const MAX_ROWS`: Most rows one insert adds.
- `const MAX_COLUMNS`: Most columns one insert adds.
- `const INSERT_SHORTCUT`: Insert rows above the cell cursor (as many as the block has), or columns to the left of the selected column headings.
- `fn column_kinds`: The kinds of empty column the add menus offer, in their words.
- `fn how_many`: A "How many" field for a menu's add or insert actions, starting at one and remembered for the session under `key` (so the next menu offers the same number).
- `fn column_name_field`: A "Name" field for new columns: empty gives "Column 1", "Column 2", …; a name is used as is for one column and numbered for several ("Rep 1", "Rep 2", …).
- `fn forget_column_name`: Clear the add menus' "Name" field once columns were added with it.
- `fn plural`: "row" or "3 rows": the object of an insert action's label.
- `fn kind_description`: What a column of `kind` holds, for tooltips.

### `crates/app-gui/src/theme.rs`

The application's own color tokens. Chosen independently; colors are never
the only cue (markers, labels and text carry the same information).

- `const SELECTED`: Selected rows: points, brush outline.
- `const DIVIDER`: Side-by-side divider at rest.
- `const DIVIDER_ACTIVE`: Side-by-side divider while hovered or dragged.
- `const ERROR`: Error text.
- `fn stale_colors`: "Source changed" marks and banner: amber text and a pale amber fill for the light appearance, or their counterparts for the dark one.
- `fn start_accent`: Accent of the start page's icons, links and highlighted cards, for the light or dark appearance (always beside text).
- `struct PlotPalette`: Colors of plots, for the light or the dark appearance.
- `fn plot_palette`: The plot colors for the appearance `ui` is drawn in.
- `struct ScriptPalette`: Colors of the script editor, for the light or the dark appearance.
- `const TICK_LABEL_SIZE`: Size of tick labels at the standard text size, in points.
- `const AXIS_TITLE_SIZE`: Size of axis titles at the standard text size, in points.
- `fn begin_plot`: Style a plot draws with: a transparent canvas (the canvas and grid are painted behind the plot by `plot_axes::PlotChrome`), the frame color, and tabular (monospaced) tick labels at text scale `scale`.
- `fn axis_title`: An axis title in the plot style at text scale `scale` in `family` (egui_plot draws titles in the body style, which [`begin_plot`] sets to the tick-label face, so the title carries its own font and color).
- `fn plot_serif`: Font family of serif plot titles (Liberation Serif, see [`install_fonts`]).
- `fn axis_title_math`: An axis title in math markup: plain text exactly as [`axis_title`], anything else set with scripts and fractions in the same font and color.
- `fn level_color`: Badge colour of a measurement level (its icon carries the level too).
- `fn row_color`: A row's own colour as plots draw it: the stored sRGB colour, with the palette's dark counterpart on a dark canvas.
- `fn row_marker`: The plot marker of a row marker.
- `fn install_fonts`: Use Inter for interface and report text and JetBrains Mono for monospaced text, with DejaVu Sans and then egui's built-in fonts behind them for symbols those fonts lack (so no character is drawn as an empty box), and Liberation Serif for plots whose plot font is serif ([`plot_serif`]).
- `fn apply_window_style`: Windows (dialogs, Settings) stand out from the reports and grid behind them: in the light theme the default window has the panels' own fill and a faint shadow, so it gets a white fill, a darker edge and a deeper shadow; the dark theme gets a slightly lighter edge.
- `fn dialog_scrim`: Colour laid over the workspace behind the dialog in front, so the eye goes to the dialog (drawn only: clicks and drops still reach the workspace).
- `fn apply_text_scale`: Set every text style to its standard size times `scale` (the user's text-size setting), in both the light and dark styles.
- `fn apply_tooltip_delay`: Wait `seconds` of stillness before showing a control's tooltip, in both the light and dark styles.
- `fn text_scale`: How much larger than standard the text currently is (1 at the standard size), for sizes and spacings that must grow with the text.
- `fn window_glyph`: A small window glyph (an outlined window with a title bar, after the open-licensed Lucide `app-window` icon), drawn with shapes at the text size, in `color`.
- `fn paint_window_glyph`: Paint the window glyph of [`window_glyph`] centred in `rect` (a square).
- `fn dashboard_glyph`: A small dashboard glyph (an outlined square split into a wide top panel and two panels below, after the open-licensed Lucide `layout-dashboard` idea, drawn with shapes), at the text size, in `color`.
- `fn paint_dashboard_glyph`: Paint the glyph of [`dashboard_glyph`] centred in `rect` (a square).
- `fn example_text_size`: Font size of example text for `scale`, independent of the current setting.

## Crate `app-model` (`crates/app-model`)

GUI-independent application logic: analysis reports, plot data and linked brushing. The egui front end (app-gui) is a thin layer over this crate.

Dependencies: `calamine`, `image`, `krilla`, `krilla-svg`, `mysql`, `odbc-api`, `postgres`, `rayon`, `regex`, `rhai`, `rusqlite`, `rust_xlsxwriter`, `rustls`, `rustybuzz`, `scraper`, `stat-bayes`, `stat-core`, `stat-data`, `stat-discrete`, `stat-doe`, `stat-functional`, `stat-inference`, `stat-linear`, `stat-mixed`, `stat-multivariate`, `stat-predictive`, `stat-quality`, `stat-reliability`, `stat-signal`, `stat-strd`, `stat-text`, `stat-timeseries`, `stat-viz`, `tokio-postgres-rustls`, `ureq`, `usvg`, `webpki-roots`, `zip`.

### `crates/app-model/src/acceptance_sampling.rs`

Acceptance sampling reports ([`stat_quality::acceptance`]). Like power
calculations, these do not read the data table: they design a lot-by-lot
inspection plan from a producer's and a consumer's risk point, and
describe it — and any plans the analyst enters for comparison — by their
operating-characteristic (OC), average-outgoing-quality (AOQ, with its
limit AOQL), average-total-inspection (ATI) and, for double plans,
average-sample-number (ASN) curves.

- `enum PlanDesign`: Which plan to design from the risk points.
- `struct AcceptanceRequest`: An acceptance sampling question.
- `struct EvaluatedPlan`: One plan in the report, with its measures.
- `struct AcceptanceAnalysis`: A computed acceptance sampling report.

### `crates/app-model/src/action.rs`

The action model: everything a person can do to an open table, as typed
values that both the desktop application and scripts apply through the
same code, and that write themselves as the Rhai call doing the same
thing (for recording and "Copy as script").

An [`Action`] works on a table's data, row states and report list (newest
report first, as the application lists them). Data changes are
[`Edit`]s; row-state actions give the whole new set (the rows selected,
excluded, hidden or coloured), so applying one twice is harmless; report
actions add, change or close one report by its position in the list.

- `enum Action`: One thing done to a table.
- `fn apply_edit`: Apply `edit` and keep `reports` pointing at the same columns: positions move with inserted and removed columns, and renamed columns keep their reports (graph canvases refer to columns by name, so only renames reach them).
- `struct RowSubsets`: A table's saved row subsets: each name with its rows (ascending), in the order they were made, and the name of the active one (whose rows alone analyses and plots use).
- `fn color_by_column`: Colour every row from its value in column `column` (by name): a colour and marker per level of a categorical column (levels named by their value labels), or the sequential ramp over a continuous column's range; rows with a missing value lose their colour and marker.
- `struct RowStyles`: A table's row colours and markers, and the column plots key them by.
- `fn color_text`: `"#rrggbb"` for a row colour.
- `fn analysis_call`: The Rhai call that runs `report` on the table in variable `var`.

### `crates/app-model/src/anom_analysis.rs`

Analysis of means (ANOM) bound to the row state
([`stat_inference::anom`]): group means, proportions or rates against
decision limits around the overall value, for one grouping column or (for
means) a balanced two-way layout.

Rows that are excluded or miss the response, size or a group value are
left out. Means: each group's rows. Proportions and rates: the event
counts (and trials or exposure, from a column or a constant per row) are
summed over each group's rows; without a group column every row is its
own group. Each charted point carries the dataset rows behind it, so
brushing a point selects its group.

- `enum AnomKind`: What kind of data is compared.
- `struct AnomRequest`: What to analyse.
- `struct AnomAnalysis`: A computed analysis of means.

### `crates/app-model/src/area_analysis.rs`

Area under a sampled curve ([`stat_inference::area`]): the trapezoid
area of the mean response at each `x` above a baseline, Bailer's (1988)
standard error from replicates, the areas above and below the baseline
and the peaks above it, one curve per level of an optional group column.

The report can save three transforms of the response as new columns:
the response minus its curve's baseline, the response as a percentage of
its curve's range (0 at the smallest value, 100 at the largest), and the
response as a fraction of its curve's total. The same transforms are
formula functions (`subtract_baseline`, `percent_of_range`,
`fraction_of_total`), which share [`curve_transform`].

- `struct AreaRequest`: Settings of an area-under-the-curve report.
- `enum CurveTransform`: A transform of a response, computed within each curve (group).
- `fn curve_transform`: `kind` of `values` within each group (`groups[i]` is row `i`'s group, numbered from 0, in row order).
- `struct AreaAnalysis`: A computed area-under-the-curve report.

### `crates/app-model/src/arima_analysis.rs`

Series and Signals ▸ ARIMA: a seasonal ARIMA(p,d,q)(P,D,Q)ₘ model
([`stat_timeseries::arima`]) fitted to one numeric column by exact maximum
likelihood, with orders chosen by the user or by the stepwise automatic
search (differencing chosen by KPSS and seasonal-strength tests, then
orders by AICc), optionally on a Box–Cox scale, with forecasts,
prediction intervals, residual diagnostics and in-sample accuracy. The
series is read and the shared sections drawn by [`crate::forecasting`].

**Inputs (transfer functions).** Other columns can enter as input series
through rational distributed lags `ω(B)B^b/δ(B)` (Box, Jenkins, Reinsel &
Ljung 2015, ch. 11–12; [`stat_timeseries::arima::transfer`]). The rows
used are those where the series and every input have values; rows after
the series whose inputs are filled in (and the series is empty) supply the
future input values the forecasts need, so the horizon is cut to what the
inputs cover. A delay left to the data is the first lag of significant
prewhitened cross-correlation between the input and the series, both
differenced as the model differences the series (for the automatic search,
as the KPSS and seasonal-strength tests difference it). The report adds
the transfer-function estimates, each input's impulse response (fitted and
estimated from the prewhitened cross-correlation) and the cross-correlation
of the residuals with the prewhitened input as a diagnostic check.

**Box–Cox.** With a λ (given, or Guerrero's choice) the model is fitted
to `(y^λ − 1)/λ` (`ln y` at λ = 0). Fitted values, forecasts and limits
are transformed back; the back-transformed point forecast is the median
of the forecast distribution, not its mean, and the standard errors stay
on the transformed scale.

- `enum ArimaOrders`: How the ARIMA orders are set.
- `struct TransferRole`: An input series of a transfer-function model: the column and its transfer-function orders.
- `struct ArimaRequest`: Columns and settings of an ARIMA report.
- `struct ArimaAnalysis`: A computed ARIMA report.

### `crates/app-model/src/attribute_agreement.rs`

Attribute measurement studies: agreement of appraisers who rate parts
into categories ([`stat_quality::attribute_agreement`]) and the bias and
repeatability of a go/no-go gauge from acceptance counts
([`stat_quality::attribute_gauge`]).

#### Data layout
The agreement study reads one row per rating (long format): a part
column, an appraiser column, the rating, and optionally a trial column
(otherwise an appraiser's ratings of a part are trials in row order) and a
standard column holding each part's known category (the same on every
row of the part; empty cells are ignored). Every appraiser must rate every
part equally often.

The gauge study reads a reference value per row with either an
acceptance count and a number of checks per row, or one row per check
with a result column, a check counting as accepted when its result is the
chosen label.

Both reports run through [`crate::ComparisonReport`]; plotted markers are
summaries, not dataset rows.

- `struct AgreementRequest`: An attribute agreement study of ratings in long format.
- `fn agreement_categories`: The categories of the rating (and standard) columns in the order used: `order` first, then any other labels in natural order.
- `struct AgreementAnalysis`: A computed attribute agreement report.
- `struct AttributeGaugeRequest`: A go/no-go gauge study: acceptances at reference values.
- `struct AttributeGaugeAnalysis`: A computed attribute gauge report.

### `crates/app-model/src/attribute_capability.rs`

Attribute capability: the fraction of defective units (binomial) or the
defects per unit (Poisson) of a process, from a count column and a sample
size column (or a fixed size), one sample per row
([`stat_quality::attribute_capability`]).

The report gives the estimate with its exact interval (and, for the
binomial, parts per million and the process Z), the p or u chart that
shows whether the process is stable enough for the estimate to mean
anything, the cumulative estimate over the samples (which should settle),
the rate of each sample against its size (which should show no trend), and
a table of the samples. Every plotted point is a dataset row, so brushing
links them.

- `enum AttributeCapabilityKind`: Which count model.
- `struct AttributeCapabilityRequest`: What to analyse.
- `struct AttributeCapabilityAnalysis`: A computed attribute capability study.

### `crates/app-model/src/attribute_chart.rs`

Attribute control charts from a count column (and a subgroup-size column
or a fixed size), one subgroup per row, bound to the row state
([`stat_quality::attribute`]): p, np, c and u charts, Laney's p′ and u′
charts for overdispersed counts, and the rare-event g and t charts (one
row per gap between events).

Rows with a count (and size) that are not excluded are charted in row
order. An optional **phase** column splits the rows into runs of equal
values, each with its own center line and limits (and its own σ_z on a
Laney chart); run rules restart at each phase. Run rules apply to the
plotted statistic (the transformed times on a t chart). Every point
carries its row, so brushing a point selects its row.

- `enum SubgroupSize`: Where the subgroup sizes come from.
- `struct AttributeChartRequest`: What to chart.
- `struct AttributeChartAnalysis`: A computed attribute chart.

### `crates/app-model/src/bayes_analysis.rs`

Bayesian analyses bound to a dataset ([`stat_bayes`]): estimation with
conjugate priors, Bayes factor tests, Bayesian linear models and ANOVA
(in [`crate::bayes_models`]) and Bayesian generalized linear and
hierarchical models sampled by NUTS (also there).

Every analysis is one [`BayesRequest`] saved as
[`crate::SavedReport::Bayesian`] and run through
[`crate::ComparisonReport`], so its settings are edited in place.

* **Estimation** (`"bayesian-estimation"`): the posterior of a mean,
  proportion or event rate, for one group, two groups (difference,
  ratio or odds ratio) or paired columns, with equal-tailed and highest
  density intervals, probabilities about a reference value and a region of
  practical equivalence, and the Savage–Dickey Bayes factor when the
  prior is proper.
* **Bayes factor tests** (`"bayes-factor"`): one-sample, paired and
  two-sample t (JZS Cauchy prior on the standardized effect δ), Pearson
  correlation (stretched beta prior on ρ) and contingency tables (Dirichlet
  priors under each sampling plan), with a robustness plot over the prior
  scale.

- `enum BayesRequest`: Settings of any Bayesian analysis.
- `struct BayesReport`: A computed Bayesian report.
- `enum EstimatedParameter`: What is estimated.
- `enum BayesPrior`: The prior of an estimated parameter.
- `struct BayesEstimationRequest`: Settings of a Bayesian estimation.
- `enum BayesTestKind`: Which Bayes factor test.
- `struct BayesFactorRequest`: Settings of a Bayes factor test.
- `const DEFAULT_T_SCALE`: Default prior scale of a t test (`√2⁄2`, "medium").
- `fn sampling_key`: Project-file key of a sampling plan.
- `fn sampling_label`: Plain description of a sampling plan.

### `crates/app-model/src/bayes_models.rs`

Bayesian models bound to a dataset: linear models and ANOVA with
g-priors ([`stat_bayes::linear`]), and generalized linear and
hierarchical models sampled by the No-U-Turn sampler
([`stat_bayes::glm`]). Both are [`crate::BayesRequest`] variants.

* **Linear model** (`"bayesian-linear-model"`): effects are coded as in
  the linear model, except that categorical factors use orthonormal
  contrasts (each level effect then has the same prior) and the effect
  list is closed under heredity. Every model that keeps heredity gets a
  Bayes factor against the intercept-only model and a posterior
  probability; effects get inclusion probabilities and model-averaged
  estimates.
* **Bayesian GLM** (`"bayesian-model"`): fixed effects coded as in the
  linear model and group (random) effects built exactly as the mixed
  model builds them ([`crate::mixed_analysis`]), with weakly informative
  priors. The report shows posterior summaries with convergence
  diagnostics, sampler diagnostics, PSIS-LOO and WAIC, trace, rank,
  autocorrelation and density plots of one chosen parameter, and a
  posterior predictive check.

- `const DEFAULT_CONTINUOUS_SCALE`: Default scale of the Zellner–Siow prior on continuous effects (`√2⁄4`, "medium").
- `const DEFAULT_CATEGORICAL_SCALE`: Default scale of categorical effects (½, "medium").
- `struct BayesLinearRequest`: Settings of a Bayesian linear model or ANOVA.
- `fn family_key`: Project-file key of a family.
- `const FAMILIES`: Every family, in menu order.
- `fn family_label`: Plain name of a family with its link.
- `fn scale_prior_key`: Project-file key of a scale prior.
- `const SCALE_PRIORS`: Every scale prior, in menu order.
- `fn scale_prior_label`: Plain name of a scale prior.
- `struct BayesModelRequest`: Settings of a Bayesian generalized linear or hierarchical model.

### `crates/app-model/src/best_subsets_analysis.rs`

Best-subsets regression ([`stat_linear::best_subsets`]) bound to the
dataset's row state.

The candidate model (predictors and effects, as in a linear model) is coded
once on the rows used, and every subset of the candidate effects is
searched by branch and bound for the best models of each size. The report
lists them with R², adjusted R², Mallows' Cp, AICc and BIC, marks the best
overall by the chosen criterion, and plots that criterion against size.
Any listed model opens as a full linear-model report.

- `struct BestSubsetsRequest`: What to search.
- `struct BestSubsetsAnalysis`: A completed search.
- `const SUBSET_CRITERIA`: Every criterion, in report order.

### `crates/app-model/src/between_within_capability.rs`

Between/within capability of one numeric column whose rows fall into
subgroups — batches in time order or parallel streams — given by a
subgroup column or by consecutive rows of a fixed size
([`stat_quality::between_within`]).

The report gives three sets of indices (within, between/within and
overall), the variance components that separate between- from
within-subgroup variation, expected and observed nonconforming rates, a
row-linked plot of the values by subgroup with the subgroup means and the
specification limits, and a histogram with the limits.

- `const BETWEEN_WITHIN_LEVEL`: Confidence level of the intervals.
- `enum SubgroupBy`: How rows are grouped into subgroups.
- `struct BetweenWithinRequest`: What to analyse.
- `struct BetweenWithinAnalysis`: A computed between/within capability study.

### `crates/app-model/src/bivariate.rs`

The joint distribution of two columns.

* Two **continuous** columns: Pearson and Spearman correlations with tests and
  95% intervals, the covariance, and a brushable scatter plot.
* Two **categorical** columns: the contingency table with margins, expected
  counts, and Pearson / likelihood-ratio tests of independence with
  Cramér's V (and a warning when expected counts are too small for the χ²
  approximation).
* One **continuous** and one **categorical** column (either order): the
  continuous variable's mean, spread and 95% interval in each group, a one-way
  ANOVA of the group means, comparisons that relax its assumptions — pooled
  and Welch t-tests of the difference (two groups) or Welch's ANOVA (three or
  more), Levene / Brown–Forsythe / Bartlett tests of equal variances, and the
  Wilcoxon rank-sum (two groups) and Kruskal–Wallis rank tests
  ([`stat_linear::group_tests`]) — and the values plotted by group with each
  group's mean marked.

Rows missing either value, and excluded rows, are left out.

- `struct BivariateRequest`: Which two columns.
- `struct BivariateAnalysis`: A computed bivariate analysis.
- `const MAX_PROPORTION_GROUPS`: Most row levels whose pairwise differences of proportions are listed.

### `crates/app-model/src/boost_analysis.rs`

Gradient-boosted trees bound to a dataset ([`stat_predictive::boost`]):
a sum of small trees, each fitted to the gradient of the loss at the
current fit and shrunk by a learning rate. Uses the shared
predictive-model sections ([`crate::prediction`]).

**Rows.** As for decision trees: excluded rows and rows missing the
response are left out; missing predictor values go the way each split
learned for them. Training rows fit the trees. Validation rows choose the
number of rounds (boosting stops once their loss has not improved for the
set number of rounds, keeping the best); with k-fold validation the
number of rounds minimizes the cross-validated loss instead, and the fit
table shows the cross-validated predictions. Test rows only measure the
model. Without validation, every round is kept.

**Importance.** The total loss reduction (gain) of each predictor's
splits, with its share and the number of splits.

- `struct BoostRequest`: Columns and settings of a boosted-tree model.
- `struct BoostAnalysis`: A fitted boosted-tree model.
